annotation.kind: direct formalization of equation (7) with an operational CGS-P family and a uniform second-order remainder

assumptions: The dimensions m and n are positive, n <= m, and one fixed real m-by-n input A has full column rank.

For every positive machine unit, an operation-linked successful normalized-range execution of Algorithm 2 (CGS-P) computes Q and upper-triangular R from the same A, including the pythagorean diagonal formula.

The arithmetic interface supplies normalized-range relative-error laws for norm, division, addition, subtraction, multiplication, square root, and dot-product operations; exceptional IEEE values and breakdown are outside the represented executions.
Every computed leading R_k has a certified two-sided inverse. The strict condition c4(m,k)*epsilonM*kappa2(R_k)^2 < 1 holds for all prefixes on one fixed positive right-neighborhood of zero.

The computed R_k norms and inverse norms are uniformly bounded on one fixed positive right-neighborhood of zero, as required to propagate a uniform second-order remainder through inverse multiplication.

Equations (4)-(5) and the reversed norm comparison from (6), which precede the selected equation (7), hold uniformly with nonnegative prefix coefficients and one radius fixed before epsilonM is selected.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p11_t3_orthogonality_defect_bound {m n : Nat} (family : P11CGSPTheorem1Family m n) (analysis : P11Theorem1ResidualAsymptotics family) : forall epsilonM : P11PositiveEpsilon, epsilonM.1 <= p11Theorem1OrthogonalityRadius family analysis -> forall k : Fin n, p11OpNorm2 (p11RectOrthogonalityDefect (p11ColumnPrefix (family.run epsilonM).Q k)) <= p11C4 m (k.val+1) * p11Kappa2 (p11LeadingBlock (family.run epsilonM).R k) ((family.run epsilonM).leadingInverse k)^2 * epsilonM.1 + p11Theorem1OrthogonalityRemainderCoeff family analysis k * epsilonM.1^2
formal_statement.plain_language: On one common small-precision neighborhood, every positive prefix of a fixed-input operational CGS-P execution family satisfies equation (7)'s spectral loss-of-orthogonality bound with the exact first-order coefficient and one second-order coefficient fixed independently of the selected machine unit.

informal_proof: For each precision and prefix, define DeltaA_k as the actual factorization residual and E_k as the actual normal-equation residual. Derive the exact page-312 inverse-conjugated defect identity, then apply spectral transpose invariance, triangle inequalities, and submultiplicativity. Substitute the uniform forms of (4)-(5), use epsilonM<=1 and the reversed form of (6) to replace ||A_k||_2^2 by ||R_k||_2^2 to first order, and use the family-wide R_k and inverse bounds to obtain a second-order coefficient independent of epsilonM. The first-order term simplifies to c4(m,k)*kappa2(R_k)^2*epsilonM.
informal_statement: Numbered equation (7) for every prefix of a fixed-input operational CGS-P family, retaining the rectangular dimensions, condition (3), spectral norm, corrected source constants, computed R_k condition number, and a uniform interpretation of O(epsilonM squared).

tier_rationale: Square spectral-norm submultiplicativity is a standard Mathlib-level fact and does not materially speed L. Both conditions must derive the rectangular inverse-conjugated identity, control four residual terms, propagate uniform second-order coefficients, use the reversed equation-(6) comparison, and assemble the all-prefix c4*kappa2(R_k)^2 result.
